Reverse DCF (WACC 8.0%, terminal growth 3.0%, EV $26.07bn, FY2025 FCF base $1.192bn) implies ~3.8% 10-yr FCF CAGR versus a 7-8% base case. Despite implied growth being below base (which is a necessary condition for INCLUDE per the mandate), the verdict is WATCH rather than INCLUDE because of capital-structure deterioration (stockholders' deficit, rising leverage) that is not captured by a static reverse-DCF snapshot: if the debt-funded buyback pace continues, WACC should rise and the implied-growth bar would move back toward or above the base case.

VRSK.scenario_basis: Starting NTM P/E 20.1x, dividend yield 1.1%. Bear: EPS growth 4%/yr (organic deceleration persists, refinancing/interest cost and litigation charges weigh), multiple compresses to ~17x. Base: EPS growth 8%/yr (buyback-driven per-share accretion continues at current pace plus high-single-digit revenue/EBITDA growth), multiple flat at ~20x. Bull: EPS growth 12%/yr (growth finally reaccelerates to the repeatedly-promised Investor Day targets), multiple expands to ~22x. Anchored to Q2'26 OCC revenue growth of 5.8%, adjusted EPS growth of 5.3% (partly buyback-driven, per Non-GAAP reconciliation), and a 6.7% YoY reduction in diluted share count.
kill_criteria: Full-year 2026 revenue or adjusted EBITDA guidance is cut below the unchanged $3,190-3,240m / $1,790-1,830m range (guidance has been flat for 2 consecutive quarters; any cut would be a first)
Consolidated net debt/adjusted EBITDA exceeds 3.0x at any quarter-end (was ~2.2x on a run-rate FY26-guidance basis as of Jun'26)
A material adverse ruling, class certification, or settlement in In re: Consumer Vehicle Driving Data Tracking Litigation (MDL No. 1:24-md-03115-TWT, N.D. Georgia) exceeding an illustrative $100m
Underlying/OCC subscription revenue growth fails to exceed 6% for two consecutive quarters despite two prior quarters of management guidance promising a 'return to Investor Day targets'
Any credit-rating downgrade of Verisk's debt, or stockholders' equity remaining in deficit for more than four consecutive quarters
key_adverse_facts: Consolidated stockholders' equity moved from +$309.0m (31 Dec 2025) to a DEFICIT of -$1,189.0m (30 Jun 2026), driven by $1,571.9m of H1'26 share repurchases funded substantially by new debt (a $999m senior notes issuance plus a $500m term loan drawn and partly repaid) rather than by retained cash flow alone
Cash fell 75% in six months, from $2,178.2m to $551.4m, while total debt rose from $4,737.2m to $4,473.5m (mix shifted from short-term to long-term via refinancing)

Net income fell 9.8% YoY in Q2'26 to $228.6m, explicitly attributed by the company to 'increases in our effective tax rate, net interest expense, and legal fees incurred in connection with ongoing litigation' - i.e. financing and legal costs, not the underlying business, drove the GAAP decline

The GAAP-vs-adjusted EPS gap widened materially in Q2'26 (13% gap, $1.75 vs $1.98) versus Q2'25 (4% gap), driven by new addbacks (acquisition-related fees $18.7m, litigation reserve $2.0m, equity-method losses $6.5m) that did not exist a year earlier - the adjusted-EPS growth story is partly an artefact of what is now being excluded, not purely operating improvement

Management has stated in three consecutive quarterly releases (Q4'25, Q1'26, Q2'26) that growth 'should return to levels consistent with Investor Day targets' without yet demonstrating a clear step-up (OCC growth 4.7% Q1'26 to 5.8% Q2'26 is directionally positive but not yet proof of the promised reacceleration)

The AccuLynx acquisition was terminated in Dec 2025 after the FTC did not complete its review by the contractual deadline - a real regulatory/antitrust setback for the M&A growth lever, not a voluntary decision
